item.observed: Stopping Python removes the public /api listener and never starts the Node server
item.title: Customers lose all API access when the Python server is stopped — the public listener is the Python proxy and only its startup launches Node on loopback port 8002

item.observed: An idle searching booking remains searching past the 30-minute deadline
item.title: Customers' unanswered bookings remain active beyond 30 minutes without app traffic — expiration is only invoked by request handlers and no scheduler runs it

item.observed: After five wrong codes, release and reaccept resets otp_attempts to 0
item.title: A driver can repeatedly guess a rider's start code and bypass the five-attempt safety limit — release resets the counter and the same driver can immediately reaccept the request

item.observed: The released booking returns in the releasing driver's Trip requests
item.title: Drivers see the trip they just released in their own request list again — dispatch never filters the released_by list

item.observed: The new OTP can equal the previous four-digit OTP
item.title: Riders may receive the same trip-start code after their driver releases the trip — the replacement is randomly generated without excluding the previous code

item.observed: GET /manifest.webmanifest has no matching manifest file
item.title: A client requesting the specified web manifest path does not receive install metadata — only manifest.json is shipped

item.observed: The expiration sweep lacks bookings index {status:1, created_at:1}
item.title: Trip polling and new bookings slow as bookings accumulate — each expiration sweep filters status and creation time without a matching index

item.observed: Estimates and bookings use haversine distance × 1.3 and vehicle speed
item.title: Customers and drivers still receive materially wrong route fares — the Node rewrite retains straight-line distance and fixed speed instead of road routing

item.observed: Car drivers see and accept all car rides and rentals
item.title: Riders can still be assigned an unsuitable vehicle or courier — Node dispatch matches only the generic vehicle type

item.observed: ADMIN_EMAIL is unset and new signups default to customer
item.title: A fresh deployment still has no usable super admin to approve drivers or manage fares — Node startup seeds fares but no admin email is configured

item.observed: GET /driver/requests exposes matching bookings across India before assignment
item.title: Approved drivers can still view unrelated customers' pickup, phone and parcel details across India — the rewritten requests route has no proximity or service-area access check

item.observed: A pricing edit between estimate and confirmation changes the stored fare
item.title: Riders can still be charged a fare different from the amount they confirmed — Node booking creation recalculates after an admin price edit

item.observed: A captured payment with a lost verify request remains pending; retry creates a new order
item.title: Customers can still pay twice after successful Razorpay checkout — the Node order endpoint creates a new order after a lost verification

item.observed: A 1-hour rental at ₹100/hour with minimum ₹299 is charged ₹299
item.title: Rental customers can still be charged more than the advertised hourly rate — the rewritten rental formula applies a separate minimum

item.observed: Gross revenue includes completed online trips whose payment is pending
item.title: Super admins still see unpaid online trips as collected revenue and earnings — Node stats sums completed fares without checking payment status

item.observed: Each uncached search calls Nominatim; typing triggers requests every 450 ms
item.title: Customers can still lose address search and be unable to book — the rewritten Nominatim calls have no global rate limit

item.observed: Two concurrent booking requests can both pass the active-booking check
item.title: Customers can still end up with two dispatched drivers — Node checks active bookings and inserts separately

item.observed: Two simultaneous accepts can both pass the driver's active-trip check
item.title: One driver can still accept two riders simultaneously, leaving a rider unserved — Node checks for an active trip separately from assignment

item.observed: Suspension blocks driver endpoints even during an ongoing trip
item.title: Suspending or demoting an on-trip driver still strands the rider — role removal blocks the Node completion endpoint immediately

item.observed: An online trip completes unpaid and the rider can create another booking
item.title: Drivers and the operator can still lose fares on online trips — Node requests payment only after completion and permits unpaid riders to book again

item.observed: A valid checkout signature alone sets payment_status to paid
item.title: The operator can still record an uncaptured Razorpay payment as paid — Node verifies the signature but not the payment capture or amount

item.observed: Two admins can concurrently demote each other after both observe two admins
item.title: The operator can still lose all super-admin access — simultaneous Node role changes each pass the last-admin count

item.observed: An online driver can create and accept their own matching booking
item.title: Drivers can still create and complete their own trips, inflating earnings and revenue — Node dispatch does not exclude self-assignment

item.observed: Credentialed cross-origin requests are allowed for any Origin
item.title: Customers' account and booking data can be exposed to an untrusted site when the browser sends their session cookie — Node reflects every CORS origin with credentials and accepts cookie authentication

item.observed: Concurrent start requests can all read otp_attempts below 5
item.title: A driver can bypass the rider's five-attempt OTP safety limit with concurrent start requests — the attempt check, increment and successful transition are not atomic

item.observed: An expired searching request can still be accepted before an expiration sweep
item.title: Drivers can accept an unanswered booking after its 30-minute limit — the accept handler checks status but never checks age or expires it

item.observed: Releasing a trip overwrites its original created_at with the release time
item.title: Customers and admins see the wrong booking date after a driver releases a trip — release replaces created_at and changes the dashboard's daily booking counts

item.observed: Visiting /book/cab sends service=cab and the Node estimate returns 422
item.title: Customers opening the requested cab-booking route still cannot get a quote — /book/cab is passed as an unsupported service to the rewritten estimate API

item.observed: Nearby counts include all online drivers of that vehicle nationwide
item.title: Riders still see unavailable drivers as nearby — Node estimates count all online drivers regardless of location or active trip

item.observed: A signed-out session's issued JWT is accepted until token expiry
item.title: A revoked user's token can still access account and trip data — Node verifies the JWT signature but never checks session revocation

item.observed: Today's earnings and daily booking buckets use UTC date boundaries
item.title: Indian drivers and admins still see early-morning trips under the wrong day — Node calculates daily totals in UTC

item.observed: Two ₹32 fares give ₹52 driver earnings but report ₹13 platform earnings
item.title: Admin platform earnings still disagree with driver payouts — Node rounds commission after summing instead of per trip

item.observed: Missing index: bookings (status, vehicle, created_at descending)
item.title: Drivers' frequently refreshed request lists slow as bookings accumulate — the Node dispatch index omits the newest-first sort

item.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (service, created_at) and (status, service, created_at)
item.title: Admins' filtered bookings view slows as trips accumulate — Node lacks indexes for service and combined filters with newest-first sort

item.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, applied_at descending)
item.title: Admins' approval lists slow as applications accumulate — Node lacks an index for status and application-date sort

item.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, online, vehicle_type)
item.title: Customers' fare estimates slow as the fleet grows — Node counts online drivers by vehicle without a matching index

item.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (customer_id, status) and (driver_id, status)
item.title: Riders' and drivers' polled active-trip checks slow as histories accumulate — Node lacks owner-and-status indexes

item.observed: Missing index: bookings (driver_id, rating)
item.title: Submitting ratings slows as a driver's history grows — Node has no index for the driver-and-rating lookup

item.observed: Saving a new name does not update drivers.name used for later assignments
item.title: Riders still see a driver's old name after a profile edit — Node booking assignments copy the stale driver application name

item.observed: Admin booking list and detail responses include customer OTPs before pickup
item.title: Customers' trip-start codes are still disclosed to administrators before pickup — Node admin booking responses do not remove OTPs

item.observed: Rating a trip updates drivers.rating but not the booking's driver.rating
item.title: Customers still see the driver's old rating after reviewing a trip — the Node booking snapshot is not refreshed

item.observed: Concurrent reviews can write an older calculated average after a newer one
item.title: Drivers can still retain an incorrect average rating after concurrent reviews — Node recomputes and writes the average non-atomically

item.observed: Saving a stale pricing form overwrites another admin's saved fare fields
item.title: Admins can still silently lose each other's pricing changes — the Node fare endpoint accepts an unversioned full snapshot

item.observed: Stats omit per-role user counts and per-status booking counts
item.title: Super admins still cannot see user counts by role or bookings for each status — the rewritten stats endpoint exposes only selected aggregates

item.observed: Missing index: users (env, created_at descending)
item.title: Admins' user-management screen slows as accounts accumulate — Node has no environment-filtered newest-first index

item.observed: Changing an online driver's role leaves their profile approved and online
item.title: Riders still see demoted drivers as available — the Node role-change endpoint leaves their driver profile approved and online

item.observed: A 500 kg parcel still receives a bike quote and can be booked
item.title: Courier customers can still book a bike for a package it cannot carry — the Node estimate and booking do not validate parcel weight against vehicle capacity

item.observed: One shared HTTP client retains upstream Set-Cookie values for later requests
item.title: One visitor can inherit another visitor's session when a host-only session cookie is relayed — the Python proxy shares a persistent HTTPX cookie jar across all users

item.observed: Approved or demoted users retain cached roles while the app remains open
item.title: Newly approved drivers still cannot go online and demoted users keep stale navigation until reload — the changed profile query has no polling or refetch on focus
